newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq stocks follow Dow's decline.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq stocks follow Dow's decline.

text.p: Nasdaq shares followed a drop in the broader markets as fears of rising interest rates spooked investors, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index lost 19.57 points or 1.54 percent to close unofficially at 1249.51. The Nasdaq index traded as low as 1241 before recovering slightly. The Dow industrials ended 140 points lower at 6741.

Stocks followed U.S. Treasuries lower after a batch of economic data convinced investors that the U.S. economy was strong enough to trigger further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, traders said. The benchmark 30-year bond fell more than one point to yield 7.09 percent.

"The 30-year bond jumping above seven percent made everyone nervous. The money center banks got hit first, then the utilities and other interest-sensitive stocks got whacked. The Nasdaq, though, didn't suffer as badly as the Dow," said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president of Unterberg Harris.
"I don't think it's the begining of a big decline, though. Volume was light and many people went home early. Things could come back Monday," Finnerty said.
Other traders said while the downdraft was a cause for some concern, there was no sense of panic on the trading floor.
"It looked bad from the outside, probably, but it wasn't that panicky down here," said one trader.
Traders stressed that Thursday's drop was not an accurate test of the market since volume was light ahead of the extended Easter holiday weekend.

"There's a light audience with very little volume. Certainly bonds had an effect on the market. But basically, there was some selling pressure and nobody was around to buy stocks when they got cheap, so the downward movement gained momentum," said Barry Berman, head of equity trading with Robert W. Baird and Co.
Thursday's drop almost erased Wednesday's rally.
Intel Corp lost 1-1/2 to 139-1/2, Cisco Systems Inc dropped 1-3/8 to 51 and Microsoft Corp slipped 1/2 to 93-3/4.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd crumbled 9-13/32 to 1-31/32 after the Calgary, Alberta-based company said its claims about its gold discovery may have been overstated.
In other news, Gartner Group Inc fell 3-1/4 to 20-3/8 after Smith Barney initiated coverage of the stock and set a second quarter earnings estimate below the Wall Street consensus, analysts said.
Overall, declining issues beat gainers 2709 to 1599 on total volume of 591 million shares.
